# Environment variables — `application-security-engineer`

<!-- generated by platform/scripts/gen_env_doc.py from distribution.yaml; do not edit by hand -->

`application-security-engineer` reads the following variables from its profile `.env` (generated as `.env.EXAMPLE` on install). All are credentials or endpoints — they are **never committed and never logged**. Set them in `.env`, then forward the names into the Kali sandbox via `docker_forward_env` in `config.yaml`.

## Reference

| Variable | Required | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN` | no | — | Optional Semgrep AppSec Platform token (pulls managed rulesets/policies; omit to run local rules only) |
| `SNYK_TOKEN` | no | — | Optional Snyk API token for SCA/known-vuln lookups (read-only; omit to use trivy/grype/osv-scanner only) |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | no | — | Optional read-only GitHub token (repo + security_events) for dependency/SCA review of repos; never a write scope |
| `NVD_API_KEY` | no | — | Optional NVD API key (raises CVE-lookup rate limit 5->50/30s when enriching advisories) |

## `.env` template

Copy into the profile's `.env` and fill real values (do not commit it):

```dotenv
# Other
SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN=   # optional
SNYK_TOKEN=   # optional
GITHUB_TOKEN=   # optional

# CVE research
NVD_API_KEY=   # optional
```

## Forward into the sandbox

Add the names (not values) to `config.yaml` so the Kali container sees them:

```yaml
terminal:
  docker_forward_env:
    - SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN
    - SNYK_TOKEN
    - GITHUB_TOKEN
    - NVD_API_KEY
```

## Handling rules

- Credentials come **only** from these env vars — never hard-coded, printed, or committed (platform Security Policy).
- Prefer **read-only / least-privilege** credentials for every integration; forward names into the sandbox via `docker_forward_env`.
- Optional vars left unset simply disable or degrade the feature that needs them.
- Rotate any credential that may have been exposed; `.env` is in `.gitignore` and must stay untracked.
